desks.title: Cold brew launch — 6-week content calendar
desks.description: Fourteen pieces across six channels for the new canned cold brew: who's making what, what's waiting on sign-off, the creative palette and the message map behind it all.
desks.brief:
## Cold brew launch — content calendar

**Brand** Ember Lane Coffee · roaster, online shop and subscriptions
**Product** canned cold brew, 4-packs and 12-packs
**Launch day** @+6d · **Calendar** 6 weeks, 14 pieces, 6 channels
**Sign-off** Nadia, for every line about caffeine or health

### The message
Our coffee, cold. Single origin, roasted for it, brewed for 18 hours. Not a sugar drink and not an energy drink.

### Goals for the six weeks
- 1,500 four-packs sold, 40% of them (600) to existing customers
- 300 subscribers add cold brew to their regular order
- 20 café partners stocking it by week 4

### Where it stands
The teaser is live and the early-access email is scheduled for @+1d. **Launch week is the crunch:** five pieces publish in week 2 and none is approved yet. Weeks 3–6 are briefed but not started — fine, as long as launch week lands.

callout.body: Five pieces publish in launch week and none is approved. Send the launch email and the blog post to Nadia together @+2d, so the caffeine claims are checked once, not twice.

desks.title: Subscription drive — week 6 performance review
desks.description: Six weeks of paid social for the half-price first bag offer: what each week cost, which creative carried it, and where the last $5,000 should go.
desks.brief:
## Subscription drive — week 6 review

**Offer** first bag half price, then a delivery every 2 or 4 weeks
**Budget** $20,000 over 8 weeks · **Spent** $15,000
**Goal** 400 paid subscribers at $50 or less each
**So far** 300 paid · $50 each, blended · 43% of trials convert

### What six weeks say
- Week 4 dipped hard: the roaster video tired in its second week as the lead ad, and cost per subscriber hit $90
- Customer videos took over in week 5 and are the best performers so far, at $35–40 a subscriber
- Trial-to-paid barely moved (40–45% every week), so the problem was never the coffee — it was the ad

### Decision this week
Put the last $5,000 behind the customer videos and two new ones, or hold some back for a refer-a-friend test? Weeks 5–6 averaged 64 paid a week — two more like that clears the goal. Even at $40 a subscriber, the last $5,000 buys 125 more: 425 by week 8.

callout.title: Recommendation: back the customer videos
callout.body: Move the remaining $5,000 to the customer videos and retire the roaster ad. Release $1,000 of it for a refer-a-friend test only if week 7 costs stay under $45 a subscriber.

notes.title: Questions for the week 7 check
notes.body:
- Are the video subscribers staying? Pull cancellations before the second bag for the week 5 cohort @+4d
- Week 6 visits up 6% on flat spend — is the cold brew teaser sending people our way?
- Is $50 still the right target if fortnightly subscribers are worth more than four-weekly?
- Ask Mia for two more customer videos before the current ones tire too
- Refer-a-friend: subscribers share their own link — we never email the friend ourselves, because we have no consent to (Spam Act)

stickies.title: Rule of thumb
stickies.body: An ad lasts about two weeks before it tires. Have the next one ready before you need it.
